claims.text: Analytical geometry is the study of geometric properties, relationships and measurement of points, lines and angles in the Cartesian plane.
claims.quote: Analytical geometry is the study of geometric properties, relationships and measurement of points, lines and angles in the Cartesian plane.

claims.text: Analytical geometry is also called coordinate geometry or Cartesian geometry.
claims.quote: also called coordinate or Cartesian geometry

claims.text: A figure is drawn on the Cartesian plane by plotting each of its vertices at the given coordinates.
claims.quote: If we are given the coordinates of the vertices of a figure, we can draw the figure on the Cartesian plane.

claims.text: A point's coordinates may be written with a comma separator, e.g. A(1,1), instead of a semicolon.
claims.quote: You might also see coordinates written as $A(1,1)$ .

claims.text: The order of the letters in a figure's name indicates the order in which its vertices must be joined: A to B, B to C, C to D, and D back to A.
claims.quote: The order of the letters for naming a figure is important. It indicates the order in which points must be joined: $A$ to $B$ , $B$ to $C$ , $C$ to $D$ and $D$ back to $A$ .

claims.text: Although a figure's vertices can be named in more than one valid order (e.g. ABCD, CBAD, BADC), the convention is to write the letters in alphabetical order, so the quadrilateral is referred to as ABCD.
claims.quote: However it is conventional to write the letters in alphabetical order and so we only refer to the quadrilateral as $ABCD$ .
